title: Cómo van las midterm elections USA 2026: proyecciones en vivo y quién va ganando hoy entre republicanos y demócratas
rawText:
Cómo van las midterm elections USA 2026: proyecciones en vivo y quién va ganando hoy entre republicanos y demócratas
Los estadounidenses se acercan a las urnas para elegir a sus representantes federales y estatales; así avanza la contienda minuto a minuto
Este 3 de noviembre se celebran las elecciones de medio término en Estados Unidos 2026. En estos comicios, los estadounidenses eligen a sus representantes en el Congreso y el Senado, además de votar por otros cargos estatales, entre los que se incluyen los gobernadores de Texas, California, Florida y Nueva York. Hasta el día de las midterms se han emitido 60.113.418 de votos (por correo y anticipado), mientras millones de ciudadanos acuden a las urnas.
- La administración Trump apeló ante la Corte Suprema de Estados Unidos para que California aparte 20.000 boletas vinculadas con personas que el gobierno federal considera no ciudadanas.
- Según un sondeo realizado por The New York Times y Siena University entre el 23 de octubre y el 1° de noviembre, los candidatos demócratas a la contienda por el Senado de EE.UU. tenían ventaja sobre sus rivales republicanos en Texas, Michigan, Maine, Ohio, Kansas y Alaska.
Midterms elections USA 2026: el minuto a minuto de las elecciones
Autores en vivo (3)
Encuestas de salida de las elecciones en Estados Unidos 2026 y quién va ganando hoy
Las encuestas de salida o “exit polls” se comenzarán a publicar este martes una vez cierren los centros de votación. Sin embargo, la última encuesta nacional de NBC News, realizada entre el 28 y el 30 de octubre, registró 52% para los demócratas y 45% para los republicanos.
En el Senado, los republicanos tienen hoy una mayoría de 53 a 47. Allí, el sondeo de The New York Times y Siena recogido en la última encuesta de las midterms mostró ventaja demócrata en seis estados:
- Michigan: Abdul El-Sayed, 53%; Mike Rogers, 42%.
- Texas: James Talarico, 50%; Ken Paxton, 43%.
- Maine: Troy Jackson, 51%; Susan Collins, 45%.
- Ohio: Sherrod Brown, 49%; Jon Husted, 44%.
- Kansas: Adam Hamilton, 49%; Roger Marshall, 44%.
- Alaska: Mary Peltola, 48%; Dan Sullivan, 46%.
Quién controla el Congreso: escaños ganados por partido
Elecciones de medio término del 3 de noviembre de 2026. Se actualiza cada minuto.
Fuente: The Associated Press. El Senado incluye las bancas que no se renuevan este año.
El demócrata Josh Shapiro fue reelecto gobernador de Pensilvania, asegurando su segundo mandato tras derrotar a la republicana Stacy Garrity, según AP.
Shapiro fue fiscal general del estado durante dos períodos y se le considera un posible candidato a la presidencia en 2028.
A las 19 hs (CT) |20 (ET) | 22 (AR) cerraron las urnas en Texas. En pocos minutos se conocerían los primeros resultados.
Yolanda Renee King, única nieta del ícono de los derechos civiles Martin Luther King Jr., votó en las midterm elections. La joven, compartió en sus redes sociales que acudió a las urnas en Atlanta junto con sus padres, Martin Luther King III y Arndrea Waters King.
A las 19 (ET) | 21 (AR) cerraron los centros en Florida. Según la proyección de AP, con el 50% de los votos escrutados, el candidato demócrata a la gobernación, David Jolly, supera a Byron Donalds con el 52,6%.
Mark Warner, senador demócrata que buscaba la reelección, ganó las elecciones del martes para el Senado de Estados Unidos por Virginia, tras derrotar al republicano Bert Mizusawa, según una proyección de AP.
Warner obtuvo un cuarto mandato en el Senado, donde se desempeña como vicepresidente del Comité de Inteligencia del Senado. Su victoria se produce en un estado con una de las mayores concentraciones de empleados federales, quienes sufrieron las consecuencias de los esfuerzos del presidente Trump por reducir drásticamente la plantilla del gobierno al inicio de su segundo mandato.
Las urnas en Florida cierran a las 19 hs (ET) | 21 hs (AR). Por tanto, se prevé que los primeros resultados se conozcan cerca de las 20 hs (ET) | 22 hs (AR) .
Según AP, se esperará hasta que cierren todas las urnas en el estado antes de declarar a los ganadores de las elecciones estatales.
Trump proclama la “Semana Anticomunista” mientras espera los resultados de las midterms 2026
A pocas horas de que comiencen a conocerse los resultados de las midterms 2026, Donald Trump firmó una proclamación que calificó como la “Semana Anticomunista”.
“Hago un llamado a todos los estadounidenses para que se mantengan firmes en su defensa contra cualquier amenaza al estilo de vida estadounidense y para que protejan nuestra ardiente llama de libertad de la oscuridad del comunismo”, se leen en el texto publicado por la Casa Blanca.
En algunos centros de votación en Chicago se agotaron las papeletas. Según AP, la portavoz de la Junta Electoral de la ciudad, Julie Metea, declaró que se imprimirían más boletas, aunque la espera para usar una máquina de votación electrónica podría ser larga.
Tres centros de votación en Pensilvania extienden su horario debido a problemas con las máquinas
Las autoridades del condado de Chester, en Pensilvania, informaron que extenderán el horario de votación en tres centros electorales después de que “problemas en la configuración de las máquinas” retrasaran la apertura de los lugares de votación, situados justo al oeste de Filadelfia, según consignó AP.
El Tribunal de Causas Comunes del condado de Chester (Chester County Court of Common Pleas) concedió a estos tres centros una extensión de 30 minutos, lo que significa que los votantes podrán emitir su voto hasta las 20.30 (ET) | 22.30 (AR) , indicó el condado.
Los votantes que acudan a estos tres centros después de las 20.30, momento en que cierran los centros de votación en todo el estado, deberán utilizar papeletas provisionales.
A través de su cuenta en Truth Social, el presidente Donald Trump expresó que seguía los resultados “previos a las elecciones” en Fox News.

title: Ten years later, ‘Pokémon Go to the polls’ still haunts the internet
rawText:
In the lead-up to a presidential election that would irrefutably transform American culture, Hillary Clinton took the stage at a rally in Virginia as she campaigned to become the first female president.
“We’re going to have a lot of jobs — jobs from building infrastructure to coding. Creating new apps,” she said. “I don’t know who created Pokémon Go, but I’m trying to figure out how we get them to have Pokémon Go to the polls.”
Ten years later, it is once again Election Day in the United States. Now, most app developers aren’t even writing their own code anymore, thanks to AI, and Pokémon Go has been sold to a company wholly owned by Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund. The only thing about that political moment that hasn’t changed is that “Pokémon Go to the polls” memes still crop up on every Election Day.
“It was very bold and confident, and also just sounded so terribly out of touch and corny,” Cesar Ruiz de Castilla, an elected ward committee member in Philadelphia, told TechCrunch. “I don’t know if the mainstream media cared that much about it, but everyone was making a meme about it and talking about it online.”
Since then, digital culture has become increasingly inextricable from the fate of American politics. Donald Trump tweeted his way through his first term, then later started his own social media platform; presidential campaigns hire meme managers; the White House invites podcasters and content creators to press briefings; Elon Musk even spun up his own advisory group under Trump that named itself after the cutesy doge meme and then slashed international aid programs.
“The 2016 election was such a monumental moment in internet history, and we were all there for it — our politics have become more, not just divided, but segmented online,” Organizer Memes, a political influencer who teaches Gen Z activists how to reach their peers online via memes, told TechCrunch. “It’s a relic of an optimistic, bygone political era.”
Now, people who weren’t even old enough to vote in 2016 reflect on the year as a cultural turning point, even calling it “the last good year.” It’s a sentiment that isn’t so much political as it is rooted in nostalgia for an era of internet culture before AI slop, when we used social media to connect with friends, rather than doomscrolling through an algorithmic feed of people we don’t even follow.
At the start of the new year, this yearning for the old internet became a viral sentiment as millions of people shared throwback photos from 2016 on Instagram.
Spotify reported that user-generated playlists featuring 2016 in their titles spiked 790% in the first three weeks of the year, and the company changed its Instagram bio at the time to say it’s “romanticizing 2016 again.”
Never mind that, at the time, the internet perceived 2016 as a cursed year, even before the election — months earlier, one Slate columnist wondered how 2016 compared to 1348, the year the Black Death took hold in Europe.
“[Pokémon Go to the polls] is in that era of the singular internet, when Facebook and Twitter and Tumblr were all kind of bouncing content back-and-forth and not just this complete anarchic mess of 25 platforms that we now have and don’t use,” Organizer Memes said.
Organizer Memes also notes that some cultural touchstones that felt more significant then — like the obsession with Harambe the gorilla — haven’t had as much staying power as “Pokémon Go to the polls.”
Perhaps this is because we’re bound to remember “Pokémon Go to the polls” every few years on Election Day, and because it appeals to both sides of the aisle. On the right, it’s a way to make fun of Democrats, and on the left, it’s a shared groan of embarrassment.
“It’s like if all the kids in a class are making a joke, and then the teacher gets in on the joke, and it stops being funny,” Mack Finkel, who canvassed at the polls on Tuesday on behalf of a healthcare workers’ union, told TechCrunch. “I think there’s a key essence of millennial cringe happening here, and it’s the same reason that all my friends are rewatching [HBO’s] ‘Girls.’”
Clinton’s decade-old, corny comment can be seen as a precursor to the “Kamala is brat” meme. While the former vice president’s record as a prosecutor initially made her unpopular among some left-leaning young voters, they rallied around her once she became the only alternative to Trump. Gen Z rallied around Harris by creating flashy, absurdist “fan cam”-style edits of the candidate’s best quips in the aesthetic of Charli XCX’s album “Brat,” which soundtracked the summer of 2024.
“Previously the views I saw about Harris were making fun of her being a cop, like her history as attorney general in California with truancy laws,” Jess Rauchberg, an assistant professor of communications at the University of Leeds, told TechCrunch at the time. “Now we see that same style of memeification, but it’s an endorsement.”
It’s hard to say why “Pokémon Go to the polls” jokes still make us laugh — whether we’re mocking Clinton or expressing solidarity with others who keep showing up to vote, even as each passing year leaves us feeling more cynical.
“Pokémon Go to the polls” is a way of urging others to make the time to vote and take Election Day seriously, while still acknowledging disappointment with aging lawmakers who don’t know what it’s like to come of age in the social media era. It’s shrouded in enough irony to project a sense of jaded detachment, yet remains a desperate, earnest plea to our friends: Please, just go vote.

title: Ferrari’s controversial Luce EV is sold out for 2027
rawText:
The Luce, Ferrari’s first electric car and one of its most polarizing models, isn’t just selling. It’s selling out.
The five-seater EV designed by Jony Ive, Apple’s longtime design chief, was mocked and widely panned when it debuted in May, sending Ferrari’s stock price lower. But all that criticism hasn’t dampened demand, according to CEO Benedetto Vigna.
The 2027 production run of the Luce, which starts at about $615,000, is “fully allocated,” Vigna said Tuesday during the company’s third-quarter earnings call, meaning every car Ferrari plans to build next year already has a buyer. “If someone comes, he has to wait one year to get the cars,” Vigna added. The first deliveries of the Luce are expected to begin in the fourth quarter.
Just how many Luce cars that represents is unclear. Ferrari has never publicly disclosed how many Luce vehicles it plans to produce. The Financial Times reported earlier this year, citing unnamed sources, that Ferrari planned to sell just under 500 units this year. The company’s longer-term target is to sell 2,500 units by 2030, or about 600 a year, according to the Financial Times.
Speculation on who these buyers are — ahem, the founders of multibillion-dollar AI labs, perhaps? — will have to remain just that Luces are spotted in the wild. Vigna wouldn’t provide a breakdown of who these Luce customers are, only noting it was a “good mix in terms of client, it is a good mix also in terms of geography.” He later added that there is no specific pattern or demographic of Luce buyers.
While Luce deliveries have yet to begin, Ferrari’s existing lineup and growing demand for personalized options helped fuel its financial performance in the third quarter. Revenue from customizations, which executives said accounted for more than 21% of revenue from cars and spare parts, helped boost profits. The company said deliveries of the F80, its limited-run hypercar, and customization reflect its clients’ “ever-deepening desire” to make each Ferrari uniquely their own. As a result, the company raised its full-year guidance, saying it now expects adjusted earnings of at least €3 billion ($3.36 billion), up from €2.97 billion.
Ferrari, which enjoys some of the highest profit margins in the auto industry, reported third-quarter revenue of €1.9 billion, up 7% from a year earlier, and net income of €431 million, up 13%. Operating profit was €563 million, for an operating margin of 29.7%, meaning the company kept roughly 30 cents of every dollar of revenue as profit from its core business.

title: Indie games are missing launch dates because Steam is backed up
rawText:
Many indie game developers have recently posted on social media about unexpectedly long approval wait times for their game submissions on Steam, with some of the approvals causing developers to miss their planned launch dates.
Indie games are missing launch dates because Steam is backed up
One developer has been waiting for weeks on approval for a game it planned to release today.
For example, Studio Daimon, the team behind an upcoming title called Food Devils, had planned to launch the game in early access today after submitting its build on October 12th. But the game is “still awaiting approval,” according to a post from game director Alfred Kamon. “Even now, we don’t know when Steam will give us the final OK to finally release our game. We sent another ticket last week saying that the situation was urgent and that we might miss our release date because of this, but it also got ignored.”
In October, publisher 2 Left Thumbs said it missed its planned launch of Wheel Make It “by nearly two weeks” due to the long wait for build reviews. You can read some details about the studio’s setbacks, including failing a review for a “one single option in the menu” not being accessible with a controller, in a Steam post. There are lots of other recent posts about review build waits as well.
Valve says on a Steam developer website that a review of a game’s store presence “typically takes 3-5 business days to complete,” though the company suggests submitting a page for review “at least 7 business days before you want it live to account for potential changes you’ll need to make.” However, as of late, Steam has seemingly been grappling with a sharp increase in games; October’s Steam Next Fest had 7,240 games, a 65.2 percent increase over June’s Steam Next Fest, according to How to Market a Game. A Reddit user also found that 49.9 percent of all games released since Valve started asking developers in 2024 to label games that use AI now have an AI disclosure.
Kamon and 2 Left Thumbs suspect the longer waits are due to “slop” slowing down the process. “We can only assume it’s because Steam’s review queue is clogged up by AI slop, but the whole process is now taking several weeks for some developers,” said Kamon.
Valve didn’t immediately reply to a request for comment.
Itch.io has also been dealing with a rise in games, with the platform saying last weekend that “The number of game pages being created per-day has doubled in the past 2 months.” Last night, the platform said it “Just deleted a couple terabytes of ai slop 😌”

title: Google’s Gemini-powered Home Speaker is already on sale for 20 percent off
rawText:
If you’re looking for a good smart speaker, the Google Home Speaker is down to around $79 ($20 off) in all four colors at Best Buy, Walmart, and Target. That’s the best price we’ve seen for the Gemini-powered speaker, which launched in June and represents Google’s first smart speaker in several years.
Google’s Gemini-powered Home Speaker is already on sale for 20 percent off
Google’s latest smart speaker offers surprisingly good sound for its size, Gemini-powered voice controls, and more.
In her review, my colleague Jennifer Pattison Tuohy noted that Google’s new Home Speaker offers a nice balance of sound quality, size, and design. It’s smaller than the prior-gen Nest Audio, making it easy to place anywhere in your home. However, despite its small size, it produces loud, clear audio with 360-degree sound. Our own David Pierce even found it sounded cleaner, louder, and sharper than Amazon’s similarly priced Echo Dot Max, though Tuohy preferred the latter’s fuller sound and stronger bass. The older Nest Audio still sounds better overall, but Google’s latest speaker takes up less space and costs slightly less.
The Google Home Speaker also offers a few useful smart home upgrades. It supports Matter and includes a Thread border router, allowing you to connect and control a wide range of compatible smart home devices. It’s also the first Google smart speaker that can double as an audio output for the Google TV Streamer 4K, letting you play TV audio through one or two speakers instead of your TV’s built-in speakers. Tuohy found it worked well and delivered clear dialogue, though sound quality varied depending on what she was watching.
One of its most notable features is support for Gemini, which is also available on older Google speakers and is much better at understanding natural language and complex requests than the old Google Assistant. In her testing, Tuohy found it could handle multiple smart home commands at once and respond to conversational requests, like turning down the air conditioner when she mentioned feeling too hot. It’s also particularly impressive at answering general knowledge questions, though it can be slow and unreliable at times. Keep in mind, too, that some features require a $10-a-month Google Home Premium subscription, including Gemini Live, which lets you have extended conversations with the assistant without repeating the wake word.

title: Última hora del accidente de trenes de Urda, en Toledo, en directo | Puente defiende la seguridad de la línea Madrid-Sevilla: “No es una infraestructura ni abandonada ni olvidada”

El ministro defiende que la línea Madrid-Sevilla “no está abandonada” | El PP, a Puente: “Su responsabilidad no es explicar accidentes mortales, es evitarlos” | El comité de empresa de Adif acuerda una huelga el 17 de noviembre por la seguridad ferroviaria
Momentos clave
El ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente, ha defendido este martes en el Congreso que la línea de alta velocidad Madrid-Sevilla “no es una infraestructura ni abandonada ni olvidada” y ha recordado que su Gobierno puso en marcha un plan de renovación de 780 millones de euros. Puente ha relatado además que el centro de control de Adif en Atocha autorizó al AVE implicado en el accidente de Urda (Toledo) a reanudar la circulación en marcha normal, pese a la caída del sistema de seguridad LZB y a que había un tren de Iryo detenido más adelante. El accidente ha dejado 69 muertos y alrededor de 200 heridos, 40 de ellos aún hospitalizados. La portavoz del PP, Ester Muñoz, ha replicado al ministro que su responsabilidad “no es explicar accidentes mortales” sino evitarlos, y la diputada de Vox Pepa Millán le ha preguntado si “puede conciliar el sueño con 116 muertes a sus espaldas”. Sumar también ha pedido su dimisión, aunque ha aclarado que no le atribuye la culpa del accidente. El portavoz de ERC, Gabriel Rufián, ha evitado pedirla y ha sostenido que un error humano “refleja un sistema de seguridad fallido”. Por su parte, el comité de empresa de Adif ha acordado una huelga para el 17 de noviembre por la seguridad ferroviaria, aunque todavía no está formalmente convocada.

Puente reitera las dudas sobre la orden del centro de control de Adif: "Yo he dicho la verdad de lo que he escuchado, con pruebas tangibles"
El ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente, se ha defendido de las acusaciones que la oposición ha vertido sobre él por señalar a posible error humano como factor determinante del accidente de Urda que causó 69 víctimas mortales: “¿Qué hubieran hecho ustedes en mi lugar? Yo llego al centro de control a las 9.40. ¿Cuál era la alternativa, disfrazarla? Más allá de los bulos, de las mentiras, de las manipulaciones interesadas, ¿hay alguna versión alternativa de los hechos a la que yo he proporcionado? Yo he dicho la verdad de lo que he escuchado, he visto y me han explicado, con pruebas tangibles”, ha espetado el ministro, que ha indicado que aún se desconoce por qué el centro de control de Adif dio esas instrucciones ni lo que influyó para ello. Asimismo, ha explicado que los trabajadores de Adif están sometidos a unas condiciones de 37 horas semanales y horas de descanso.
El ministro ha explicado por qué cayó el LZB, lo que provocó que el control del tráfico ferroviario recayera sobre el centro de Atocha: “Cayó por un fallo de comunicación entre tres ordenadores que deben de estar perfectamente sincronizados y al no ser totalmente coherente la información el sistema se para”. Así, ha intentado ahondar en las posibles causas: “La autopsia del suceso aún no se ha hecho porque la empresa debe de percibir un permiso judicial que no sabemos si ha obtenido. Tengan en cuenta que solo han pasado seis días”.
“De las 170 incidencias de LZB que se han producido este año, 64 han afectado a la circulación”, ha indicado el ministro, que ha enumerado las que se han producido en años previos, todos entre las 69 y las 87: “Las incidencias con afectación a la circulación varían a través de los años”. Así, ha reiterado que todos los sistemas dependen de ordenadores y balizas, así que “cuando se produce un daño en las infraestructuras que soportan esos sistemas, los sistemas se caen y entra en funcionamiento el centro de control”, ha señalado Puente.
Néstor Rego (BNG) compara la tragedia de Urda con la de Angrois y carga contra la “hipocresía” del PP
El diputado del BNG, Néstor Rego, ha tachado de “obscena” la intervención de la portavoz del PP, Ester Muñoz. “Es de una hipocresía y demagogia increíble después de su actuación en Angros, donde se premió a la ministra responsable [Ana Pastor] con la presidencia del Congreso, no hubo investigación a fondo, Feijóo vetó hasta cuatro veces una comisión de investigación en el parlamento y culpó al maquinista del accidente”, ha señalado Rego, quien ha denunciado el “pacto de silencio entre PP y PSOE entonces.
El portavoz nacionalista ha reclamado una investigacion independiente y a fondo, además de actuaciones para reforzar la seguridad y la modernización de líneas como A Coruña-Lugo y A Coruña-Ferrol. “Fuimos prudentes, la prioridad era atender a víctimas y familiares. Pasdo ese primer momento, señor minsitro, es inevitable asumir responsabilidades”, ha reclamado también Rego.

La secretaria general de Podemos, Ione Belarra, ha protagonizado de nuevo una intervención muy dura contra el Gobierno, en este caso contra el ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente. “Tres de los cuatro accidentes de alta velocidad más mortíferos de todo el mundo se han producidoen España y los gobiernos de PP y PSOE han tratado de convencernos de que han sido una tragedia que no se podía evitar, un error humano (...) title: Saliba's back for Arsenal - how does Arteta solve his defensive dilemma?
rawText:
Saliba's back for Arsenal - how does Arteta solve his defensive dilemma?
- Published
Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta will soon have a big defensive dilemma.
But it is one that will be both welcome to the Arsenal boss and the envy of other top teams across the continent.
That's because William Saliba - a key figure in the Gunners' title win last season - is back in training, having missed the entire campaign so far because of a back injury following his early withdrawal in France's World Cup semi-final loss to Spain.
The 25-year-old has been one of the Premier League's top defenders in recent seasons but - in his absence - summer signing Ezri Konsa has stepped in seamlessly to help Arsenal back to the top of the table.
Indeed, since Konsa's arrival from Aston Villa for Â£55m, he and Gabriel Magalhaes have struck up a formidable partnership, with Arsenal again boasting the league's tightest defence, conceding just five goals in nine games.
Saliba had been managing his back issue throughout last season but was sent to see a specialist after the World Cup.
It was decided he did not need to undergo surgery but would require a lengthy rehabilitation. No timescale on his return was set.
The France international had been doing individual training at Arsenal's base but has now returned to full training before their Champions League meeting with Slavia Prague and then, a busy festive schedule looming.
Saliba and regular partner Gabriel were a huge reason why the Gunners won the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years last season.
Their partnership was the bedrock of Arteta's team, which conceded only 27 league goals. Saliba was then named in the PFA team of the year for the fourth consecutive time.
Arsenal have always said that they will be cautious with Saliba's return but his return to fitness will leave Arteta with some tough choices to make in his backline.

  - Published7 days ago
- How Arteta is getting the best from Rice 
  - Published10 hours ago
Konsa's excellent start
Such was Arsenal's strength in defence, there were questions about whether they needed to sign Konsa when the Gunners decided to spend Â£55m on the England international.
But the centre-back has been one of the club's best players this season as they sit top of the Premier League.
Some have even suggested Konsa and Gabriel have become the best partnership in world football, external.
Arsenal already had seven senior defenders when they signed Konsa including one of the most solid and well-established partnerships in world football in Saliba and Gabriel.
But in Saliba's absence, Konsa has started seven of Arsenal's nine Premier League matches, having joined just hours before their opening match against Coventry before coming on against former club Aston Villa for his debut.
And Arteta has said the way that Konsa has settled for the Gunners has been "unbelievable".
The defender made 286 appearances for Villa after joining in July 2019 from Brentford and helped them win the Europa League in May, the club's first European trophy since 1982.
He has established himself as a first-choice starter for England and started seven of the eight games the Three Lions played at the World Cup.
And what could now prove a big clue to his Arsenal future - he started the quarter-final against Norway at right back.
Konsa is an imposing figure, quick across the ground, and his aggression in challenges has impressed supporters.
The 29-year-old scored the opener against Everton in Arsenal's 2-0 win and put in another commanding performance as the Gunners beat Liverpool at Anfield for the first time in 14 years on Sunday.
What could Arteta do?
Arsenal host Hull on Saturday before the next international break starts this month.
That time will allow Saliba to further build up his fitness before he will become a regular option again for Arteta.
However, when Saliba does return, Arteta is going to have to disappoint someone.
Ben White and Jurrien Timber have been Arsenal's first choice right-backs this season and are dependable top-level options.
Both have previously had fitness issues but White has been available for all but one of Arsenal's games this campaign.
Konsa could move to right-back, a position he also made his England debut in, which would allow Saliba to slot in next to Gabriel in his regular spot.
Arteta values physicality in his Arsenal side and moving Konsa, who is physically imposing, to right-back would give opposition attackers a formidable challenge.
Saliba's return also lowers the chance of game time for young centre-back Cristhian Mosquera and his low number of minutes so far this season will raise questions about his future, even though he has recovered from a hamstring injury.
The Gunners played 63 games in all competitions last season as they won the league and reached the Champions League final.
And, with Arteta aiming to defend the title and have European success this time out, there will be a lot of games for him to rotate his many options.

title: Brazil publishes first global ‘roadmap’ for phasing out fossil fuels
rawText:
All countries can start to break their dependence on fossil fuels now without needing to wait for new technologies or economic changes, Brazil’s government has said ahead of a global climate summit.
Brazil, the host of last year’s UN climate conference, set out the world’s first global “roadmap” for phasing out fossil fuels on Tuesday, showing that countries could boost their economies and pull people out of poverty while breaking the link with coal, oil and gas.
But Joeri Rogelj, a professor of climate science and policy at Imperial College London, said that although the Brazilian roadmaps represented a step forward, they were limited. “The roadmaps are valuable but fall short of clearly indicating the pace of change needed by including no timeline or key benchmarks,” he said.
“Because of this omission, they still leave much to be imagined about what is needed to achieve the Paris agreement’s ultimate goal: limiting global warming to well below 2C, and preferably to 1.5C, to avoid dangerous climate harm.”
André Corrêa do Lago, Brazil’s president of the Cop30 summit, said the roadmaps were intended to help move the annual UN Cops away from their previous focus on negotiating global agreements to tackle the climate crisis, and on to implementing the targets that had already been agreed. Cop31 takes place in Antalya, Turkey, this month.
“They are documents of implementation,” Corrêa do Lago told the Guardian in an interview. “There is a different group of people that negotiate and that implement. The problem we’ve had at many Cops is to think that the same people who negotiate might also need to coordinate the implementation – this is not the case.”
He said the roadmaps should be taken up by ministries of finance, transportation, energy and infrastructure to work on how they could be implemented in each country.
Brazil hosted the Cop30 summit last November in the coastal city of Belém, in the Amazon rainforest, where a bitter dispute broke out over whether the final set of resolutions should include pledges on fossil fuels. As a compromise, the presidency agreed to produce two roadmaps, one on “transitioning away from fossil fuels in energy systems in a just orderly and equitable manner” and the other on halting and reversing deforestation.
These roadmaps are separate from similarly named plans from governments that met after Cop30 at a conference in Santa Marta, Colombia, in April, to discuss the transition away from fossil fuels. At that conference, nearly 60 countries formed a new “coalition of the willing”, separate to Cops, to set out their own national roadmaps to phase out fossil fuels. Several countries have since produced national plans, including Germany, France and the Netherlands.
The roadmaps produced by governments under the Santa Marta initiative are much more specific and prescriptive than Brazil’s, as each of those is written by the national government responsible for implementing the policies recommended.
The Brazilian roadmaps only set out steps that are possible. They are not binding, they contain no deadlines or milestones for actions, and they leave it to countries themselves to “diagnose” their degree of dependence on fossil fuels and select steps to reduce it.
“Every country will have a different rhythm [for moving away from fossil fuels] – it’s very important to concentrate on the diagnoses of countries’ circumstances,” Corrêa do Lago said. “Based on these diagnoses, they can choose their levers [of policy] and implement the transition.”
Among the steps Brazil suggests is for oil and gas producers to urgently cut the flaring and venting of gas from extraction sites. Methane is a greenhouse gas 80 times more powerful than carbon dioxide, so this would have an immediate impact. Other steps are for countries to reduce their subsidies to fossil fuel use or production, and building up renewable generation.
The roadmap on deforestation notes the large sums that are expected to be needed to help poor countries with heavily forested areas such as the Amazon, the Congo rainforests and south-east Asian tropical forests that are under threat from fires and palm oil exploitation.
About $300bn is likely to be needed every year for forests by 2030, and $500bn a year by 2050, according to the roadmap, citing UN figures. The current amounts available fall far short at about $85bn a year.
At Cop30 last year, Brazil set up the Tropical Forest Forever Facility, a fund aiming to preserve forests, which raised about $7bn from various countries including a £400m loan from the UK.
The deforestation roadmap also notes the importance of regulating trade between forested countries and consumer countries. At present, there are few trade checks to stop unscrupulous companies from selling goods from deforested areas.
In some cases, deforestation has appeared to be condoned or encouraged by local or even national administrations. Indonesia is being sued by civil society groups for “gross negligence” over the record-breaking fires over the last few months that have cleared swathes of forest and destroyed wildlife habitats, most likely to be replaced by palm oil plantations.
Brazil was able to publish the roadmaps after its president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, won a fourth election term just over a week ago. In the last four years under Lula, deforestation rates have fallen by about 70%. His defeated opponent Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the jailed ex-president Jair Bolsonaro, had been expected if elected to return to his father’s policies of rampant exploitation of the Amazon rainforest.

title: FC Barcelona vs. Aston Villa HOY: Horarios y dónde ver la Jornada 4 de Champions League
rawText:
El FC Barcelona vuelve a la Champions League con una prueba exigente frente al Aston Villa de Unai Emery. El conjunto de Hansi Flick busca recuperar terreno en la competencia europea, pero tiene que resolver un problema que condiciona sus planes: las numerosas bajas en defensa. El equipo inglés llega con paso perfecto en el torneo en una prueba contra un contendiente al título.
La cuarta jornada de la Liga de Campeones también ofrece encuentros atractivos. Bayern Múnich visita al Atlético de Madrid, el Manchester United recibe a la Roma y el Inter de Milán se enfrenta al Feyenoord. Además, el PSG se mide al Villarreal, en una cartelera que reúne a varios protagonistas del futbol europeo.
¿A qué hora juega Barcelona vs. Aston Villa y dónde ver HOY la Champions League?
El partido entre FC Barcelona y Aston Villa se disputa este martes 3 de noviembre de 2026, en el Spotify Camp Nou, como parte de la cuarta jornada de la fase liga de la Champions League.
El silbatazo inicial está programado para las 14:00 horas, tiempo del centro de México. La transmisión del juego estará disponible a través de HBO Max y TNT.
- Partido: Barcelona vs. Aston Villa
- Instancia: Jornada 4 de fase de liga, Champions League 2026/27
- Fecha: Martes 3 de noviembre de 2026
- Hora: 14:00 horas, tiempo del centro de México
- Sede: Spotify Camp Nou en Barcelona, España
- Transmisión: HBO Max y TNT
¿Cómo llegan Barcelona y Aston Villa al partido de Champions League?
El Barcelona llega después de golear 6-1 al Deportivo Alavés en LaLiga, resultado que representó una reacción tras las derrotas frente al París Saint-Germain (4-2), en Champions, y el Real Madrid (2-1), en el campeonato español.
Sin embargo, Hansi Flick tendrá que lidiar con seis ausencias. Andreas Christensen, Eric Garcia, Xavi Espart y Jules Kounde están lesionados en defensa, mientras que Dani Olmo y Roony Bardghji tampoco estarán disponibles. En la previa, el entrenador alemán reconoció que administrar tantas bajas no es sencillo, aunque aseguró que ve a sus jugadores convencidos.
“Tenemos cuatro defensas fuera, jugadores de calidad, y no es fácil de gestionar”, explicó Flick. También destacó la disposición de Frenkie de Jong y Brian Fariñas para ocupar posiciones defensivas cuando el equipo lo necesita.
Aston Villa llega con tres victorias consecutivas en la Champions League y 12 goles anotados. El delantero senegalés Nicolas Jackson ha contribuido con tres tantos en el torneo.
Unai Emery reconoció la dificultad del compromiso y colocó al Barcelona entre los cinco principales candidatos al título europeo. “El Barcelona es favorito para ganar esta competición. Es uno de los cinco equipos con más opciones de ganar la competición”, afirmó en conferencia.
El entrenador español también tiene un historial complicado frente al conjunto catalán: suma tres victorias, seis empates y 21 derrotas en 30 enfrentamientos. Uno de esos tropiezos fue la remontada del Barcelona ante el PSG en 2017, cuando el equipo azulgrana ganó 6-1 después de perder 4-0 en la ida.
¿Qué otros partidos de Champions League se juegan el martes 3 de noviembre?
La actividad del martes comienza desde las 11:45 horas con dos partidos: Shakhtar Donetsk contra Sporting CP y Galatasaray frente al Stuttgart. A partir de las 14:00 horas se disputan los siete encuentros restantes de la cartelera.

title: Transportes reduce el tráfico entre Madrid y Sevilla para separar más los trenes hasta que esté en pie el nuevo sistema de seguridad ERTMS
rawText:
Transportes reduce el tráfico entre Madrid y Sevilla para separar más los trenes hasta que esté en pie el nuevo sistema de seguridad ERTMS
El paquete de medidas de seguridad anunciado por el ministro Puente tras el siniestro de Urda incluye una doble supervisión por parte de los controladores del tráfico de cada orden enviada a los maquinistas
El tráfico de trenes en la línea de alta velocidad Madrid-Sevilla va a reducirse por orden del Ministerio de Transportes al menos hasta las primeras semanas de 2027. Se trata de obtener una mayor separación entre los convoyes, a modo de distancia de seguridad, hasta que entre en operación el sistema de señalización ERTMS nivel 2 en sustitución del más anticuado LZB, según ha anunciado el ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente, en su comparecencia ante los medios tras el Consejo de Ministros de este martes. Una caída del LZB está en en el origen de la tragedia del miércoles 28 de octubre en Urda (Toledo), donde perdieron la vida 69 personas por un choque entre trenes. Esa tecnología alemana fue estrenada en 1992 en el Corredor Sur, donde se quedó arrinconada ante la generalización del ERTMS en el resto de líneas de altas prestaciones por tratarse del estándar europeo que permite el tráfico transfronterizo.
Puente comprometió el pasado viernes, en una comparecencia previa ante la prensa, una revisión del funcionamiento de todo el sistema en la Madrid-Sevilla. Este martes, cuando aún no se ha cumplido una semana desde el accidente, ha desplegado un programa de actuaciones que incluye nuevas tecnologías en los centros de control del tráfico de Adif; modificaciones en los protocolos de control y seguridad del tráfico, y mejoras en las condiciones de trabajo del personal de la referida Adif en la veintena de centros de control repartidos por el país, cuatro de ellos para la alta velocidad. Se trata de acercar el máximo posible a cero el riesgo de coger un tren; también de recuperar la confianza de los viajeros.
El de Urda ha sido el segundo siniestro de extremada gravedad en diez meses en el corredor Madrid-Sevilla, tras el ocurrido en Adamuz el 18 de enero con un balance de 46 fallecidos. Este martes, a las 17.00, el ministro comparece en el Congreso para dar explicaciones sobre las circunstancias que han rodeado al de la semana pasada. La oposición urge la dimisión de Puente y de la cúpula de Adif. El titular de Transportes dice ver lógica esta demanda desde múltiples esferas, pero no la acepta en boca del líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo. Este mediodía ha estado muy presente la gestión del Gobierno popular del accidente de julio de 2013 en Santiago de Compostela, en la curva de Angrois. Puente asevera que su actuación no admite comparaciones con la de Ana Pastor, por entonces ministra de Fomento.
Otras de las iniciativas destacadas, entre el ramillete elevado al Consejo de Ministros, son la instalación de un nuevo software para los centros del control del tráfico, el uso de la inteligencia artificial para la supervisión del sistema, y la conclusión, lo más rápido posible, del citado despliegue del referido ERTMS Nivel 2 entre Madrid y Sevilla. La caída del LZB a las 8.30 del miércoles motivó la parada de seis trenes en el entorno de la estación de Urda y, posteriormente, una serie de órdenes a los maquinistas contrarias al reglamento ferroviario. Los minutos de confusión concluyeron con el choque de dos trenes en el kilómetro 118, un AVE de Renfe y una unidad de Iryo que permanecían detenida por problemas técnicos, ambos con dirección Andalucía.
En este último caso, el de las comunicaciones emitidas desde el control a los trenes, Transportes ha promovido la modificación de los protocolos de gestión del tráfico para incluir mecanismos de validación cruzada. Cada una de las decisiones que se tomen en un centro de Adif en momentos de circulación “degradada” (cuando no se cuente con la asistencia de sistemas de bloqueo automático que ofrece el LZB o ERTMS) va a estar supervisada y tendrá que ser validada por, al menos, un segundo controlador. Hasta ahora, valía con el telefonema (comunicación oficial de seguridad) dictado por un solo operario.
Teniendo en cuenta los audios de las comunicaciones mantenidas entre el centro de Madrid-Atocha y los maquinistas durante la crisis de tráfico en Urda, al AVE que chocó con el Iryo detenido en Urda, en el kilómetro 118 con sentido Sevilla, se le transmitió marcha normal a las 8.36 (seis minutos después de la caída del LZB). De este modo podía alcanzar 200 kilómetros por hora en su avance hacia la tragedia, que se produjo a las 8.53. El telefonema o protocolo aplicado fue el LZB4, mientras que el reglamento exige marchar a la vista (a menos de 40 kilómetros por hora), tal y como recoge el protocolo LZB3.
El gestor de la infraestructura Adif está supervisando estos días cómo se actuó en sus centros de control del tráfico cada vez que se ha caído el sistema de seguridad en la linea Madrid-Sevilla, el anticuado LZB. El ministro de Transportes desveló el viernes que la tecnología que sirve para separar trenes, y activar el frenado automático en caso de emergencia, ha fallado en 170 ocasiones en lo que va de año, 14 de ellas en los 25 kilómetros que separaban al AVE e Iryo accidentados. Puente ha anticipado que “puede haber algún caso excepcional” en que se reinició el tráfico de trenes aplicando un protocolo contrario al reglamento ferroviario, como sucedió en Urda. En todo caso, ha añadido, “parece que no se trata de un comportamiento sistémico”. El modus operandi de Adif cuando falla el LZB es uno de los pilares de la investigación técnica y judicial. Se trata de dirimir si el fallo del operario fue puntual o respondía a la fuerza de la costumbre.

title: NBC News Exit Poll: How it works and how we use the results on election night
rawText:
Before votes are tallied on election night, exit polls offer an early look at who is voting and what is motivating their choices.
An exit poll is a survey of voters taken as they leave (or exit) their voting location. Unlike public opinion polls ahead of elections that predict whether respondents will vote, exit polls capture the views of voters in person on Election Day. The exit poll also reflects the views of people who voted early or by mail — we take steps to reach those voters by phone and by mail, as well as online.
Here’s how exit polls work, where they are conducted and how NBC News will be using the results on election night and in the days after.
Who conducts the exit poll?
For this year’s midterm election, exit polls are being conducted by SSRS, a survey and market research firm, on behalf of a group of news organizations: NBC News, ABC News, The Associated Press, CBS News, CNN, Fox News and MS NOW. The companies receive the same data, and NBC News then independently analyzes and reports on the exit poll results.
What questions are asked?
The national exit poll asks respondents whether they voted for the Democratic or Republican House candidate in their district, and in many states the poll also asks which candidates voters supported in Senate and governor’s races.
In addition, the poll usually includes a number of questions about voters’ views, such as, “What is the most important issue facing the country?”
The other key component of an exit poll is asking about voters’ demographics, such as age, gender, race and education level.
These types of questions help illustrate how different groups of people voted and what mattered to them. Demographic data is also used to weight the exit poll — that is, to make sure the poll reflects the demographics of the electorate as well as the election results.
The national and state exit polls include some different questions, to capture voters’ views on local issues and candidates.
The news organizations jointly determine how the exit poll will be conducted and develop the questionnaire together.
How are exit polls conducted?
The in-person Election Day exit polls are surveys that voters in scientifically selected precincts are asked to fill out as they leave their polling place. The paper forms have about 25 questions.
This year, interviewers will be stationed at over 450 polling locations in 15 Senate battleground states. Each interviewer follows local rules about where they can stand outside the polling location.
The exit polls also include a pre-election survey to capture voters no matter how they participate, whether early, by mail or on Election Day. Before Election Day, respondents are surveyed through methods including mailed invitations, telephone and text interviews and online surveys. Interviewers then follow up with respondents to confirm that they voted and whom they ultimately voted for.
Respondents can complete the poll in English or Spanish.

Interviewers phone in the results from the questionnaires to a data center three times during the day. Those results are tabulated with the pre-election survey results, and the exit poll is updated throughout the day as new data is collected.
Are exit polls anonymous?
Yes. In person, voters fill out the questionnaires themselves and deposit them in boxes, so their answers, like their actual ballots, are secret. Interviews conducted by mail, by phone and online do not retain any personal information about the voter who was interviewed.
Which states will have exit polls?
In addition to a national exit poll, which captures voters in all 50 states, there are also state exit polls this year in 45 states that have consequential Senate and governor’s contests.
How many people are interviewed?
The national exit poll sample will include over 75,000 voters at voting locations, online and by telephone.
In 15 states, interviewers will be stationed outside at least 30 randomly sampled voting locations. In the remaining states, interviews are conducted via phone, online and mail.

The sample size in Alaska will be about 3,000 voters, and it will also include interviews from voters at early-voting locations before Election Day.
All other states with exit poll results for Senate and governor’s races will include between 500 and 3,000 voters.
How do we use exit polls?

title: NASA smashed into an asteroid. Now Hera is closing in to see what happened
rawText:
NASA smashed into an asteroid. Now Hera is closing in to see what happened
- Date:
- November 3, 2026
- Source:
- European Space Agency (ESA)
- Summary:
- Europeâs Hera spacecraft has captured its first clear view of two asteroids involved in NASAâs historic 2022 experiment to redirect a potentially dangerous space rock. Now approaching the pair, Hera will investigate the mysterious aftermath of the collision and uncover why the asteroid shifted far more than scientists predicted.
- Share:
The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft has reached an important milestone in its mission to investigate a historic asteroid collision. For the first time, its onboard camera has captured the two asteroids Didymos and Dimorphos as separate objects rather than a single point of light.
The asteroid pair is currently about 197 million kilometers from Earth. Hera obtained the new image on the evening of October 18 using its black-and-white Asteroid Framing Camera, while the spacecraft was approximately 1,280 kilometers from its targets.
"With this image, the smaller Dimorphos asteroid becomes visible for the first time," explains Michael Kueppers. "Before this acquisition, the spacecraft was still resolving the Didymos system as a single dot. But now, even though Dimorphos is made up of only around one pixel in this initial image, it is clearly well separated from its parent body."
Hera Closes In on Two Asteroids
The breakthrough image follows a successful series of maneuvers designed to slow Hera as it approaches the asteroid system. Earlier in October, the spacecraft fired its thrusters twice, with one week between the maneuvers. These adjustments reduced its speed relative to the asteroids to just 20 meters per second, allowing mission controllers to carefully manage the remaining approach.
Although the two asteroids appear tiny in the initial image, they are substantial objects. Dimorphos measures about 151 meters across, making it roughly comparable in size to the Great Pyramid of Giza. Its larger companion, Didymos, is approximately 780 meters in diameter, slightly smaller than the height of Dubai's Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building.
Dimorphos travels around Didymos at an average separation of just 1.15 kilometers, moving at a speed of approximately 18 centimeters per second.
"For the very first time we are seeing through Hera's own eyes the very double asteroid system that the mission was designed and built for," adds mission manager Ian Carnelli.
"Our views will grow much sharper as Hera comes closer. We will unveil the first detailed images of Dimorphos -- the first object in the Solar System to have had its orbit measurably shifted by human action -- on 25 November."
Uncovering the Aftermath of NASA's Historic Asteroid Collision
Hera's arrival will give scientists an opportunity to examine the results of a groundbreaking planetary defense experiment conducted four years earlier.
On September 26, 2022, NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) spacecraft deliberately collided with Dimorphos at approximately 6.1 kilometers per second. The impact blasted debris as far as 10,000 kilometers into space and shortened the asteroid's orbital period around Didymos by roughly 33 minutes.
The experiment demonstrated that a spacecraft could deliberately change an asteroid's motion, an achievement with potentially enormous implications for protecting Earth from future asteroid threats.
However, the collision also produced results that scientists are still trying to fully explain. The asteroid's orbital change was substantially greater than computer simulations had predicted, raising questions about its physical properties and how it responded to the impact.
Researchers still do not know whether DART left a crater on Dimorphos or significantly altered the asteroid's overall shape. They also need more precise measurements of its composition, internal structure, and mass to understand why the collision was so effective.
Answering these questions is essential for transforming the 'kinetic impact' approach into a reliable planetary defense strategy.
Hera Prepares for a Detailed Asteroid Investigation
Over the coming months, Hera will carry out a detailed 'crash site investigation' to uncover what NASA's collision actually did to Dimorphos.
The spacecraft will use a collection of scientific instruments to examine the asteroid and its surroundings. It will also release two small satellites, known as 'CubeSats', each approximately the size of a shoebox, to gather additional observations from much closer distances. The investigation is expected to eventually include landing operations.
Together, these measurements should help scientists better understand how asteroids respond to high-speed impacts and improve predictions of how future deflection attempts might work.
Meet the Hera Space Companion
Anyone interested in following Hera's journey can explore the mission through the Hera Space Companion. More than a conventional AI chatbot, this interactive communication platform is connected to the mission and designed to make the European Space Agency's first planetary defense mission accessible to the public.

title: Tenerife striker De Miguel dies after on-field collision
rawText:
Tenerife striker De Miguel dies after on-field collision
- Published
Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel has died after the 30-year-old suffered a serious injury during a Spanish second-division match.
The forward suffered head and chest injuries during a match against FC Andorra on Monday in a heavy collision with goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who was sent off for his challenge.
De Miguel's condition was described as 'stable but serious' on Monday but his health deteriorated on Tuesday morning, with the Spaniard dying at 07:00 GMT.
Reuters reported on Tuesday that police in Spain have opened an investigation for possible involuntary manslaughter following De Miguel's death.
Under Spanish law, any death that is deemed non-natural automatically triggers a judicial inquiry.
"Heartbroken, with a lump in our throats and unable to believe this is true" Tenerife said.
"There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing that can lessen this overwhelming sadness. We stand with his grieving family, with his loved ones, with all of Tenerife who mourn this cruel loss today."
'There are no words'
Tenerife and Andorra were drawing 2-2 seven minutes into stoppage time when the incident occurred.
Owono ran towards the centre circle to clear a long ball when his knee appeared to collide with De Miguel.
The striker lay motionless on the pitch as medical staff treated him before he was taken by ambulance from Tenerife's Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez to hospital.
Players from both teams were visibly distressed by the incident, with a number of De Miguel's team-mates in tears.
The referee showed Owono a straight red card before abandoning the match.
The goalkeeper, who had over 30,000 followers on Instagram on Tuesday morning, has since deactivated his account.
Spanish media, including Marca, reported De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest in the ambulance and was resuscitated by paramedics on the way to hospital.
Tenerife's president, Felipe Minambres, says the club's players will need "professional assistance" to help deal with the ordeal of one of their team-mates dying.
"We are all feeling vulnerable and deeply saddened right now. It's hard to even believe what has happened," said Minambres.
"We know, especially the players and the players' partners, that we will need support. We've already begun receiving offers of help today, and that support will continue.
"We will need professional assistance, but we also need the support of all our fans, because they are likely feeling the same way we are today."
Minambres added it had been a "truly unbelievable situation" and "an enormous tragedy that we have had to endure".
Andorra, Tenerife's opponents on Monday, issued a statement later on Tuesday which spoke of the club's shock and expressed condolences to De Miguel's family, club "and all those who were close to him".
"We are deeply affected by what has happened and we share the pain that the club is experiencing," it continued.
"From the very beginning we have maintained contact with them and we are at their disposal for anything they may need.
"What has happened has had a huge emotional impact on our players, the coaching staff and everyone at FC Andorra. These are particularly difficult times for everyone and we want to make sure that no one has to face them alone. That is why the club is providing psychological support to anyone who needs it."
Former Barcelona defender Gerard Pique, who co-owns Andorra, said: "I am sorry with all my soul. Rest in peace, Jesus."
De Miguel's former club, Castellon, said: "It's hard to find words when reality strikes in such an unfair way.
"We join with all our affection in the grief of his family and loved ones, whom we embrace in these terribly difficult moments and to whom we extend our most heartfelt condolences."
Javier Tebas, president of La Liga, said: "Today, we all share the terrible pain of an irreparable loss.
"My deepest condolences to his family, loved ones, team-mates and the whole club."
Real Madrid and France striker Kylian Mbappe wrote on his social media: "Much sadness, there are no words."
Inter Miami and former Barcelona forward Lionel Messi said: "There are no words. My condolences and lots of strength to all his family and friends."
The Spanish football federation announced following De Miguel's death that Tuesday's Spanish Cup fixtures had been postponed.
Two fixtures in the first round of the men's Copa del Rey were due to be played, while Espanyol were set to take on AS Celtas in the women's Copa del Reina competition.
A lower-league player with an eye for goal
De Miguel, who was born in Madrid, started his career at Leganes in 2015 and went on to play for eight different clubs in Spain.
After spells with Lugo Fuenlabrada and Internacional Madrid, he returned to Fuenlabrada before stints at Union Adarve, Navalcarnero and Unionistas.
He joined Castellon in 2023 and scored 16 goals as the club achieved promotion to Spain's second division a year later.
The Spaniard joined Tenerife on a three-year deal in 2025 and scored 11 goals in 29 appearances for the side.
De Miguel is survived by his daughter, Carla de Miguel Fernandez, who was born in 2025.

De visita en Buenos Aires, donde vino a presentar El desierto de nosotros mismos (Caja Negra), su último libro, Éric Sadin (Francia, 1973) afirma que muy recientemente descubrió que tiene una misión: ayudar a los más jóvenes a recuperar una tradición letrada y unas posibilidades de emancipación que, asegura, nos están siendo escamoteadas por un mundo tecnológico abocado a reemplazar no solo nuestras capacidades físicas, sino también las intelectuales y creativas.
“La Argentina tiene una cualidad que no se ve en otras partes; un interés por el otro, la atención, el cuidado –comenta el pensador francés, autor también de La siliconización del mundo– .Tienen conciencia de necesitar a los demás. Y es que somos más ricos con el otro. Somos más alegres con el otro; eso, para mí, es la Argentina. También las relaciones sociales táctiles. La gente te abraza, te besa, te toca. Y ahora llegamos a un estado de representaciones mentales, a un estado de la psiquis de los jóvenes donde todo esto se aparece como una ficción. Sentirse traicionado es muy hiriente. Sentirse traicionado por la sociedad, por los adultos, ¿qué es lo que produce en la psiquis? Rencor, sensación de abandono. Y te voy a hablar de lo que más me importa.
–¿Qué sería eso?
–Que abandonamos a nuestros hijos. Los hemos abandonado. Cuando se lanzó el ChatGPT, la IA generativa, en 2022, cientos de millones de individuos se abalanzaron sobre esas máquinas y dijeron “esto es espectacular, escriben en lugar de nosotros”. Lo que vimos en la escuela fue un caos total, profesores que están librados a sí mismos, el lobby de quienes quieren instalar sistemas de IA generativa y adaptar la educación a eso, lo que es una falta terrible. Nosotros no nos adaptamos a máquinas que nos van a privar de la facultad de la escritura, y en cambio dejamos a los chicos usarlas. Es nuestra culpa. ¿Te das cuenta lo que se viene? Si hay un sistema que con un chasquido de dedos o un prompt escribe en mi lugar". Esa pregunta no nos la hicimos y es una falta inmensa. Hay generaciones futuras que tendrían que juzgarnos post-mortem.

Al final de unos días, unas semanas, les resultó incómodo tener a esa chica, no sabían qué hacer, entonces la entregaron a la administración pública. Tampoco allí sabían qué hacer con ella; la soltaron y unos días después la encontraron muerta en el campo. Cómo avanza el voto anticipado horas antes de las midterms 2026
Hasta las 14 hs (ET), se emitieron 56.144.276 votos anticipados a nivel nacional, según el reporte diario de NBC News. De ese valor, 24.2 millones fueron por correo y 31.9 millones en persona.

La organización de derechos civiles sostiene que su presencia podría intimidar a los votantes. “No tienen ningún papel ni derecho a estar dentro de nuestros centros de votación”, dijo Kristen Clarke, asesora legal de la Naacp, en un comunicado.

Avanza la contienda por la gobernación de Florida. Según la encuesta realizada por el Center for Public Opinion Research (CPOR, por sus siglas en inglés) de la Universidad Stetson, el candidato republicano, Byron Donalds, lidera la contienda con un 51% frente al 45% del demócrata David Jolly.

Por su parte, Trump no celebrará mítines presenciales, pero sí participará de varios eventos virtuales para sus candidatos, según informó NBC News.

title: Fossilised red blood cells found in 115m-year-old dinosaur’s bone, say scientists
rawText:
It could be the opening of a Jurassic Park rip-off: scientists examining ancient dinosaur bones find what appear to be fossilised red blood cells, and traces of the molecule that gives the beast’s blood its distinctive crimson hue.
But that is what researchers are claiming to have discovered after analysing the hind leg bones of a small, meat-eating dinosaur called an Aratasaurus that lived and died in what is now north-eastern Brazil 115m years ago.
Electron microscope images of the dinosaur bones revealed small, round structures that resemble red blood cells in fine channels where blood vessels once ran, while chemical tests identified the presence of heme, the organic compound that allows haemoglobin in blood to carry oxygen around the body.
Such claims are controversial because biological tissues and molecules can break down fast, leaving little or no trace in ancient fossils. But if confirmed, it would open up entirely new avenues for scientists, allowing them to investigate dinosaur blood, metabolism and even their activity levels.
“We are seeing a mineral and molecular echo of the dinosaur’s original biology,” said Prof Kliti Grice at Curtin University in Western Australia who led the research team. “Fossilised red blood cells with distinct chemistry related to heme have never been found in situ in any fossil, let alone a dinosaur. This is a world first.”
The fossilised remnants of the Aratasaurus were discovered in a mine in 2008 and have since been held in the National Museum of Brazil, where researchers continue to study them. While analysing the dinosaur’s hind leg bones, Grice spotted the structures that resembled red blood cells.
The scientists’ suspicions that they were looking at red blood cells were bolstered when chemical tests came back positive for heme and its breakdown products. Tests also found traces of the amino acid building blocks for collagen, a key protein in connective and other tissues.
If the structures really are fossilised red blood cells, as the researchers contend, it raises the question of how they were preserved. According to Grice, a manganese compound called hausmannite, which formed in and around the blood cells, may have lent a helping hand by stabilising them prior to fossilisation. The same process might have helped preserve the amino acids, she added. The study appears in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
The work is already stoking debate. Prof Mary Schweitzer at North Carolina State University in the US, who has discovered remnants of blood vessels and soft tissues in dinosaur fossils, is not convinced Grice and her colleagues have found red blood cells. One reason for her doubt is that the dinosaur’s red blood cells should have a “nuclear bulge” making them appear dome-like on both sides. The structures Grice found are concave, suggesting they might be something else.
Schweitzer was more persuaded by the discovery of heme and collagen amino acids in the bone and said there was so much more to learn from exceptionally well-preserved fossils. Schweitzer added: “The conventional wisdom in palaeontology that all endogenous organics would disappear in a million years or less is being routinely challenged, and will continue to be as technological approaches to palaeontological specimens are more routinely applied.”
Another question the research raises is what other biological material might lurk in fossils collections around the world. On this, Grice urges extreme caution, adding that her work does not imply that large biological molecules such as proteins or DNA live on in ancient fossils. “Any extraordinary claim needs extraordinary analytical evidence,” she said. “The aim isn’t to find Jurassic Park DNA, it’s to determine how much genuine molecular information deep time can preserve.”
“The really exciting implication is that extraordinary molecular information may already be sitting in museum collections around the world, waiting for us to ask new questions of old fossils,” she added.

title: UK was ‘vehement’ slavery reparations should not be on Commonwealth summit agenda
rawText:
British officials reportedly insisted that discussions of reparations for slavery should not be on the agenda of the Commonwealth leaders’ summit in Antigua and Barbuda – and even warned that Andy Burnham would not attend the meeting if the subject was formally included, according to a leading Caribbean political figure.
Ralph Gonsalves, a former prime minister of St Vincent and the Grenadines and a senior figure in the reparatory justice movement Repair Campaign, welcomed Britain’s decision to enter structured dialogue on reparations, but said the UK had come “kicking and screaming” to the conversation.
Currently, slavery reparations is not on the official agenda of the Commonwealth Heads of Government (Chogm) summit, which begins on Sunday.
Trade, climate resilience and finance, sustainable debt, democracy and investment in opportunities for young people are among the stated priorities for the 56-nation bloc spanning Africa, Asia, the Caribbean and the Americas, the Pacific and Europe.
“My understanding from informed circles is that Britain was vehement not to have the matter on the agenda. The British officials – and in that regard they were joined by the Canadian officials – were even raising the prospect that if it is on the agenda the prime minister of Britain wouldn’t go,” Gonsalves told the Guardian.
“They also started to circulate this untruth that India didn’t want it on the agenda, but that was not so at all. India was very supportive at the UN general assembly resolution on March 25th, 2026. So they were spreading this false word about India.”
Gonsalves said that the relentless campaign by Caribbean nations, amplified by a growing regional and global reparations movement, has propelled reparatory justice to the heart of the political conversation at the meeting.
“Because of what happened at the UN, because of what happened in Africa, what happened in the Caribbean, and all the work which is taking place in Britain itself too, inside of the British parliament, inside of the British Labour party, both in the Commons and the House of Lords, it is an issue which you can’t duck any more,” he said.
He added: “The danger of not putting it formally on the agenda is what we see happening now, that everybody who could have foreseen, whether or not it’s formally on the agenda, even the nature of how the discussions take place at the Commonwealth, and certainly in the retreats, it would have been raised.”
Gonsalves said while the actual structured dialoguewas unlikely to happen at Chogm, it was expected that when the leaders met in their private retreat, the format and details of the dialogue would be discussed.
He said: “The British government, they’re coming, kicking and screaming to the table of structured dialogue. But at least they’re coming.”
An FCDO spokesperson said: “We categorically reject this completely untrue accusation. The UK has approached this conversation in good faith, and we have at no point told any other Chogm member what should not be on an agenda.
“Our position on reparations is clear but this government respects the right of others to raise matters as they wish.”
Prof Sir Hilary Beckles, chair of the Caribbean Community (Caricom) Reparations Commission, had described the meeting as “the Chogm of reparations”, adding that reparatory justice was “the number one item” for the Caribbean as Commonwealth leaders gather in the region.
On Friday there was a historic shift in Britain’s position when the British prime minister went further than any of his predecessors by agreeing to structured dialogue and to consider an apology.
Though Caribbean governments and campaigners welcomed Burnham’s announcement, made in an op-ed for the Guardian, it was clear that agreeing on forms of reparations was still a priority for the region.
Guyana’s president, Irfaan Ali, welcomed Burnham’s statement and called for a Commonwealth subcommittee to work out the details of the dialogue over the next six to 12 months.
“I’m happy that finally the discourse has moved to a position where it should have been, where the British government is involved, because that’s the state we are dealing with,” he said.
Ali said the talks should move beyond attempting to put a price on the indignity of slavery and towards addressing its developmental consequences.
“How do we identify a system of support where the UK government, with its financial institutions, can sit with countries … and work on a development pathway, identify development gaps, whether in health, education, social services, infrastructure?”
Barbados’s prime minister, Mia Mottley, thanked Burnham for “breaking new ground”, while making clear that the two sides remained divided. “On reparations in particular, our views differ, and we will say so plainly and respectfully,” she said.
Mottley identified an apology, investment in health and education, tackling systemic poverty and inequality, and fairer debt terms among areas where agreement could be reached.
The Bahamas prime minister, Philip Davis, said the talks were not simply about “historical remembrance” but “the enduring consequences of slavery and the importance of justice, acknowledgment and meaningful redress”.
As the meeting kicks off on Sunday, the 45th anniversary of Antigua and Barbuda’s independence from British colonial rule, King Charles is indicating he will not follow Burnham and offer a full apology, there is still a sense that the reparations fight is far from over.
King Charles and Burnham will be greeted with protests as they travel through Antigua’s capital, St John’s, to attend Chogm events.
On billboards, placards and T-shirts, in letters and at a candlelight vigil for the thousands of Africans trafficked to Antigua and Barbuda during the transatlantic slave trade, the message from the Caribbean will be clear: there will be calls for an apology and reparations.

title: Poll: Voters demand change and a check on Trump, fueling a steep Democratic midterm advantage
rawText:
Democrats have a sizable advantage in the battle for control of Congress days ahead of the midterm elections, a new national NBC News poll finds, with voters clamoring for change and voicing all-time high disapproval of President Donald Trump.
Registered voters prefer a Democratic-controlled Congress by a 7-point margin, with Democrats leading Republicans 52%-45% — 2 points more than in last month’s poll. That includes a 21-point lead among independents.
Three percent of voters remained undecided as the poll was conducted from Oct. 28 to Oct. 30, and how they shift in the final days could tilt the outcome in dead-heat House and Senate races around the country. While the overall poll suggests that Democrats are poised to capitalize on a well of dissatisfaction with the president and his policies, there are findings that complicate the favorable picture.
When it comes to which party better handles key issues, voters give Republicans and Democrats about even marks, and the Democratic Party remains deeply unpopular. Meanwhile, Republican voters in GOP-held districts and in states Trump won in 2024 are sticking with their party — which is notable because much of the battle for control of both the House and Senate runs through this red terrain.
But there are also numerous signs of trouble for the GOP, with Trump at the center of a difficult political environment for Republicans and their slim majorities in both houses of Congress. The president’s disapproval rating has climbed to 60%, a new high mark in the NBC News poll across his two terms, and his approval rating stands at 40%.
After Trump won a second term in 2024 promising to bring down prices and restore the economic conditions of his first term, roughly 3 in 4 voters head into the midterms dissatisfied with the state of the economy. Nearly two-thirds of voters are calling for a change from the direction Trump has been leading the country, with 50% calling for “a great deal” of change, a new high mark in NBC News polling data.
And for the first time in 30 years of NBC News polling, more voters say they are dissatisfied with their financial situation (51%) than satisfied (49%).
“The Trump presidency can be summarized as the promise of two years ago and the peril of two days from now,” said Democratic pollster Jeff Horwitt of Hart Research Associates, who conducted the survey with Republican pollster Bill McInturff of Public Opinion Strategies.
Horwitt noted Trump returned to the White House after promising economic prosperity and peace. But now voters are expressing widespread concerns about the economy, with prices rising during the Iran war.
Amid those concerns, 64% of voters — including a third of Trump voters — say the president has fallen short of their expectations, with 34% saying he has lived up to them. Seventy percent of voters say the country is on the wrong track, a 9-point increase over the last year.
Voters continue to rank inflation and the cost of living as the most important issues facing the country, followed by government corruption, threats to democracy and immigration and border security.
“Democrats are in total control of the 2026 issue agenda,” said McInturff, the Republican pollster, noting that only voters who think immigration is a top issue are breaking for his party right now.
Democrats have a 1-point advantage on which party would better control inflation, a slight decline from September but still a warning sign for the GOP, which led on the issue in 2024. Republicans have a 2-point advantage on the economy, a marked decline from the party’s double-digit advantage on the issue in recent years.
Voters are also signaling that they are fired up about the midterms, with 70% ranking themselves as a “9” or “10” on a 10-point scale of interest in the election. Democrats have a 12-point advantage among those most-engaged voters, while Republicans have a 2-point edge among voters who are less interested in the election.
Self-described MAGA Republicans also say they’re significantly more interested in the election than Republicans who don’t identify with the MAGA wing, as Trump and his party push to turn out voters who typically sit out midterm elections.
That dynamic could be one reason why Republicans have leaned into culture war arguments in key races, attacking Democrats on transgender issues. The new poll shows a potential limitation of that strategy: Democrats have a 5-point advantage on the question of which party would better handle transgender issues, despite those Republican attacks.
It’s not all good news for Democrats, and the poll contains fresh signs that a number of voters are pushing back on the GOP, as opposed to falling in love with the Democratic Party, which remains deeply unpopular.
Just 29% of voters view the Democratic Party positively, while 38% have positive views of the Republican Party. Around half of voters have negative views of both parties.
Still, some voters who are wary of Democrats are still planning to support them this year.
“Republicans have proven that they are not to be trusted. So I would rather see the balance of power shift, than maintain one party’s control,” one poll respondent from Texas, who voted for Trump in 2024 and is supporting Democrats for Congress this year, said in an expanded response.
“I don’t trust Republicans or Democrats, really,” the man added.
Republican disappointment
Frustrations among voters like that man from Texas, who backed Trump in 2024 and typically backs Republicans, are dragging down the president and GOP candidates this year.
